title: Quench of chiral superconductivity by quantum phase fluctuations in twisted cuprate bilayers
authors: Yin Shi, Mengxian Zhao, Fei Yang, Miao Liu, Sheng Meng
abstract: Following theoretical proposals of chiral $d+id'$ superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers, experimental signatures of time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) remain highly controversial. Here we demonstrate that quantum phase fluctuations fundamentally reshape the phase diagram of this proposed chiral state. Unlike regular superconducting orders, the chiral $d+id'$ state requires long-range coherence of an interlayer phase degree of freedom and is therefore intrinsically vulnerable to phase fluctuations. Incorporating these fluctuations nearly eliminates the chiral phase over most parts of the phase diagram, restricting it to a narrow twist-angle window and ultra-low temperatures. The fluctuation-driven destruction of chirality produces a first-order transition into the $d$-wave state, giving rise to coexistence and metastability. Meanwhile, Josephson phase locking is strongly weakened at the TRSB quantum critical point, which sits well within the superconducting regime. More broadly, our work establishes quantum phase fluctuations as a fundamental constraint on the emergence of TRSB phases in low-dimensional layered quantum materials.
summary: The paper theoretically examines the stability of proposed chiral d+id' superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers against quantum phase fluctuations. The key finding is that these fluctuations severely destabilize the chiral state, forcing a first-order transition into a more conventional d-wave phase at low temperatures. This establishes quantum fluctuations as a critical constraint on realizing exotic superconducting symmetries in layered materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum phase fluctuations fundamentally alter the predicted phase diagram of chiral d+id' superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers, particularly concerning Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking (TRSB).
main_result: Quantum phase fluctuations strongly suppress the stability of the chiral state, confining it to narrow windows of twist angle and ultra-low temperatures. This leads to a first-order transition into the regular d-wave state.
method: The authors derived the fluctuation-corrected free energy by integrating out long-wavelength phase fluctuations from a continuum microscopic model Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is twisted cuprate bilayers, modeled using a continuum approach incorporating interlayer tunneling and Coulomb repulsion. The analysis focuses on how collective phase fluctuations renormalize the superconducting order parameters.
key_observables: Minimal superconducting gap (2Delta_min), relative phase angle (2varphi), Josephson coupling strength (Delta_J), and the stability region in the twist-angle vs. Temperature plane.
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($T/T_{1L}^c \lesssim 0.016$), specific interlayer tunneling strengths ($t$), and the twist angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis treats phase fluctuations by integrating out long-wavelength modes, which is appropriate for low temperatures; it also uses a simplified local form for the interlayer coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how quantum phase fluctuations renormalize the free energy and equilibrium phase angle across different twist angles, showing the suppression of the chiral state's stability region.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by developing a fluctuation-corrected free energy functional for the superconducting order parameters. It then analyzes this functional to map out the resulting phase diagram in terms of temperature and twist angle, comparing mean-field predictions with fluctuation corrections.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how collective quantum fluctuations fundamentally constrain exotic superconducting phases (like chiral superconductivity) predicted by simpler theories, which is relevant for understanding emergent order parameters in strongly correlated systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic of a twisted bilayer superconductor, where each layer alone is a d-wave superconductor, and the two layers are coupled through electron tunneling with an amplitude t. αk is the polar angle of the momentum k. The superconducting phase of each layer can be decomposed into a static part ±φ and a dynamical part ηl(r, τ) (dependent on the imaginary time τ). A nonzero φ (not integer multiple of π) signifies d + id′ chiral superconductivity. Crucially, fluctu- ations in the dynamical phases could renormalize the equilib- rium φ. (b–d) Free energy density (vertically shifted to match minima) with (blue solid line) and without (orange dashed line) phase fluctuations at zero...

FIG. 2. Phase diagrams in the twist-angle–temperature plane with (left panel) and without (right panel) phase fluctuations for t = 10 meV. The false color represents the minimal super- conducting gap. The phase diagrams are symmetric about θ = 45◦. T 1L c is the superconducting transition temperature of a monolayer. The horizontal dotted line in the left panel indicates the lowest temperature reached in existing experi- ments [11]. The white line in the right panel delineates the normal–superconducting phase border, while the d–(d + id′) border is obvious by the false color.

FIG. 3. Phase diagrams in the tunneling-amplitude– temperature plane with (left panel) and without (right panel) phase fluctuations. The twist angle is fixed at 45◦. The false color represents the minimal superconducting gap. The dot- ted line marks the realistic tunneling amplitude t = 10 meV. Note the different scales of the y axes.

FIG. 4. Josephson gap with (left column) and without (right column) phase fluctuations for t = 10 meV. The dashed line delineates the d–(d+id′) border for the mean-field case, while such a border is obvious by the false color for the phase fluc- tuating case.
